edges.description: Mutant-transfected cells show raised activating Tyr419 phosphorylation and negligible inhibitory Tyr530 phosphorylation, and co-transfecting wild type with mutant still raises Tyr419 substantially, which is the heterozygous case.

edges.description: Embryos injected with mutant src grow significantly smaller bones, and src-depleted embryos grow larger ones, matching the direction of the human osteoporosis against the osteopetrosis of SRC loss.
edges.limitations: Larval bone at 5 days post-fertilisation is not adult bone remodelling, and the model works by transient mRNA overexpression rather than a heterozygous germline allele at endogenous dosage.

edges.description: Thrombocyte numbers fall in mutant embryos, but the mechanism this node states cannot be modelled in zebrafish at all.
edges.limitations: Zebrafish thrombopoiesis has neither megakaryocyte endomitosis nor proplatelet formation with loss of the nucleus, so a reduced thrombocyte count in this model is not evidence about proplatelet formation. The reduction in GFP-positive thrombocytes also did not reach statistical significance on triplicate injection.

edges.description: Deleting Src raises bone density; the human gain-of-function allele lowers it. The model establishes that SRC activity sets osteoclast resorption, and nothing more about this disease.
edges.limitations: Loss of function rather than gain, homozygous rather than heterozygous, and the direction of the bone phenotype is reversed. These mice have normal platelet counts and no bleeding, so the model says nothing about the haematological disease.

edges.description: Shows that a bone phenotype arising from SRC-family loss can by itself displace haematopoiesis from the marrow. The direction of the bone change is again the reverse of the human disease.
edges.limitations: Double loss of function in two kinases, against a single heterozygous gain-of-function allele in patients; the splenomegaly here follows osteopetrosis, while in patients it follows myelofibrosis.

nodes.description: Mucocutaneous bleeding such as epistaxis, petechiae and menorrhagia, and bleeding after tooth extraction. Bleeding is mild in some families: in the third kindred bleeding scores were not consistently above normal.

nodes.description: SRC is required for osteoclast bone resorption, and loss of Src causes osteopetrosis in mice, the opposite of the osteoporosis in patients. The discovery report suggests that the balance of podosomes, which also precede osteoclast resorption, may explain the opposite bone phenotypes. The human bone mechanism has not been studied directly.

nodes.description: Glu527 sits next to Tyr530, the C-terminal tyrosine whose phosphorylation holds SRC in its closed, autoinhibited conformation. The E527K substitution is predicted to break that clamp, and the variant protein shows raised kinase activity and activation-loop Tyr419 phosphorylation. In patient platelets the active form of SRC predominates and overall tyrosine phosphorylation is increased.

nodes.description: The genes deleted are mouse Src, the ortholog of human SRC (hgnc:11283), and mouse Hck, a second Src-family kinase that no report implicates in this human disease. Also loss of function, and included only for the marrow-environment result: severe osteopetrosis in these mice drives extramedullary haematopoiesis, anaemia and leukopenia, and transplant experiments show the defect lies in the marrow environment rather than in the stem cells.

Variant megakaryocytes extend few proplatelets. The defect is reproduced by transducing normal stem cells with the variant and is partly restored by an SRC kinase inhibitor. The platelets made are few, dysmorphic, variable in size and poor in alpha granules.

They form abundant immature megakaryocytes that make almost no proplatelets, and a SRC inhibitor partly restores proplatelet formation. This is the closest thing to the human mechanism anyone has put in a dish.
Despite constitutive SRC activity, patient platelets respond poorly to collagen while spreading more on fibrinogen, giving a mild platelet function defect on top of the low count.

Three members of the founding pedigree were also splenectomised, and there the platelet count and morphology did not correct. Recorded because it was done and because the genetic diagnosis is what prevents it being done again on the wrong indication, not as a recommended treatment.

nodes.description: The gene deleted is mouse Src, the ortholog of human SRC (hgnc:11283). A loss-of-function model, the opposite perturbation to the human disease. It is included because its bone phenotype is the mirror image: these mice develop osteopetrosis from osteoclasts that cannot form ruffled borders, where patients lose bone. That opposition is what ranked SRC first in the phenotype-matching search that found the gene.
Lifelong thrombocytopenia from childhood, the one feature shared by all reported carriers; counts vary widely, from about 38 to 139 x 10^9/L in the third kindred.

nodes.description: The only in vivo model in the disease direction. Mutant mRNA is injected into embryos, which then show reduced thrombocytes and smaller bones; a SRC inhibitor in the fish water prevents the bone change. The gene bound here is zebrafish src, the ortholog of human SRC (hgnc:11283); E525K is the zebrafish residue corresponding to human E527K.

The only reported disease allele, found in the founding pedigree, as a de novo variant in a second family, and in a third kindred. Molecular modeling predicts loss of autoinhibition, and the variant raises SRC kinase activity and Tyr419 phosphorylation when overexpressed.
